agent.description: The agent-neutral manifest `frob agent sync` publishes into each coding agent's home.

hooks.description: Hook registrations, each `"NAME:EVENT:MATCHER"` naming a `hook` item.

items.description: Canonical items, each `"KIND:NAME = SRC"` (kind: instruction, hook, agent, skill, support).

busy_timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds a connection waits on a locked cache database.

base.description: Ref the diff of a `--ticket` run (SCOPE001, TICK002) is taken against.

exclude.description: Glob patterns of paths no rule inspects.

fail_on.description: Lowest severity that makes `frob check` exit 1; `none` never fails.

fail_on_unresolved.description: Which Unresolved findings fail the gate: `required`, `never` or `all`.

output_cap_bytes.description: Bytes a sibling or tool may print on one stream before it is killed (default 64 MiB).

process_spawners.description: Crates (directories under `crates/`) allowed to spawn processes; empty turns `PROC001` off.

require_siblings.description: When true an unusable configured sibling is a required Unresolved (`SIB001`).

sibling_timeout_secs.description: Wall-clock bound in seconds of one sibling `check --json` run (sibling-contract.md section 7).

size_cap.description: Files larger than this many bytes are skipped.

telemetry.description: Append one JSON line per run to `.frob/telemetry.jsonl`.

ticket_hops.description: Hops of dependents (callers, via the symbol graph) added to a `--ticket` run.

tool.description: External tool stages run after the built-in rules, outside the time budget.

claims.description: How long a claim may sit idle before it is evictable (`[claims]`).

agent_idle_hours.description: Hours a claim held by an agent (`FROB_AGENT` set at claim time) may sit idle; 0 means never evict.

class.description: Per-class idle windows in days (`[claims.class]`); they override `idle_days`, and 0 means never evict.

expedite.description: Days an expedite claim may sit idle: a critical fix must not be parked on someone's absence.

intangible.description: Days an intangible claim (chores, debt) may sit idle: slow upkeep gets a longer leash.

count.description: `all` counts every calendar day as idle time; `weekdays` skips Saturday and Sunday.

evict_agent.description: `auto` lets `frob work --next` evict an idle agent claim when nothing else is claimable; `confirm` never does.

evict_human.description: `auto` lets an idle human claim be evicted without a confirmation (design D-4); `confirm` makes `frob claim evict` need `--yes` for a human holder.

evict_rate.description: Most automatic evictions one clone performs per local calendar day.

idle_days.description: Calendar days a human claim may sit idle before it is evictable; 0 means never evict.

max_hold_days.description: Longest hold, in days, `frob claim hold` accepts.

paused_max_days.description: Longest stretch, in days, a blocked, review, train or CI pause stops the idle clock.

soft_max_windows.description: Consecutive windows soft-only activity (touch, comment, empty commit) may keep a claim alive; 0 means soft activity never extends a claim.

warn_at.description: Fractions of the window (each above 0 and below 1) at which the holder is warned.

compute.description: The substrate `[compute]` knobs every product reads (architecture.md section 6).

dynamic_calls.description: How a dynamic call is treated.

effects.description: How an undeclared effect is treated.

expansion_steps.description: The macro and template expansion step budget.

normalization.description: How an unnormalizable construct is treated.

notebook_order.description: How a notebook with an undeclared cell order is treated.

public_signatures.description: How an unannotated public signature is treated (`warn-unresolved` or `required`).

directives.description: Which directive namespaces are honoured (code-model section 4, decision D63).

namespaces.description: Comment namespaces the scanner reads; comments in any other are ignored.

evidence.description: How evidence is captured and where large blobs go.

allowed_tools.description: Programs the `command` provider may run (the first word of the command must be listed); the `pytest`, `vitest`, `jest` and `dotnet` providers need their own name listed too.

attesters.description: Identities (git `user.email`) that may attest a criterion; `frob init` and `config sync` write the repository owner's email, and an empty list means nobody may.

path.description: Path of the `dotnet` executable the provider runs; empty finds `dotnet` on `PATH`.

inline_max_bytes.description: Transcripts up to this many bytes are stored inline in the event file.

nextest_profile.description: Value for `cargo nextest run --profile`; empty leaves nextest's own default.

report_fields.description: Per-tool report field for the `command` provider: tool name to the dotted path of the executed-test count in the JSON the tool prints on stdout (for example `jest = "numTotalTests"`); a listed tool that ran no test is refused, an unlisted tool is UNMEASURED for granular evidence (exit code only).

store.description: Blob store: `dir:<path>` (relative paths start at the repository root, `.git/` at the common dir) or an `https://` URL (recorded only).

timeout_secs.description: Wall-clock limit in seconds for one provider process.

editor.description: Path of the Unity editor executable the provider runs, used whatever `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt` says; empty looks for the version that file names under Unity Hub's standard install locations.

gc.description: Garbage-collection settings: what the throttled pass may reclaim and how much to keep.

artifact_retention_days.description: Evidence blobs under `.git/frob/artifacts` older than this many days and unreferenced by an open ticket are removed.

cache_budget_mb.description: Budget in MiB of the regenerable caches under each checkout's `.frob/`.

enabled.description: Run the automatic pass at all; `frob doctor --fix` still runs it on request.

guard_min_free_gb.description: Free GiB below which a pass runs regardless of the interval; 0 turns the guard off.

incremental_max_age_secs.description: Remove build incremental directories not used within this many seconds.

interval_secs.description: Minimum seconds between automatic passes (the stamp lives under the git common dir).

keep_binaries.description: Binary names (without extension) whose build output is never collected.

keep_recent_secs.description: Artifacts within this many seconds of the newest one belong to the latest build and are kept.

land_target_budget_gb.description: Budget in GiB of the repository-shared `land-target` under the git common dir; the oldest units go first and the latest build's are never evicted.

target_budget_gb.description: Per-checkout build-output budget in GiB; the oldest artifacts are evicted past it; `frob work` links each new worktree's `target/` to the shared `land-target`.

time_limit_secs.description: Wall-clock bound in seconds of one pass; the rest waits for the next one.

worktrees.description: Remove worktrees of closed tickets and of expired leases with nothing unsaved.

cas_retries.description: Compare-and-swap retries when moving a ledger ref.

grimble.description: The `[grimble]` table: model roots and binding policy (grmb-spec 3, binding.md 6).

large_lines.description: A function, method or type longer than this many lines fires LARGE001; 0 turns the rule off.

modeled.description: Selectors whose public units must have an owner (SYS005); empty turns the rule off.

models.description:
Root `.grmb` files, one independent model each; only files reachable from them through
`include` are loaded (MDL019 names the rest, MDL021 fires when none is declared).

rename_min_tokens.description: A Body with fewer tokens than this cannot be paired as a rename (binding.md 5.4 item 3).

strict.description: Warn rules SYS001 and SYS005 become Errors.

invariants.description: Architecture invariants enforced over the import graph (INV002).

forbid_imports.description: Imports no file matching `from` may contain; each entry needs a `reason`.

land.description: The `[land]` table: which base CI checks gate a land and what an unreadable state does.

block_on_unknown_ci.description: When base CI cannot be read: false reports it as Unresolved and lands anyway, true refuses.

ci_ignore.description: Check-name patterns that never block a land (publish and release jobs by default, which test no code).

ci_required.description: Check-name patterns (`*` wildcard, case-insensitive) that count toward the gate; empty means every check.

require_base_green.description: Refuse a land whose base tip has a failing required CI check; false turns the whole gate off.

train.description: Land ready tickets as batches on the merge train; false makes `land --train` land one ticket at a time.

train_max.description: The most tickets one train batch may hold.

lease.description: Knobs of the lease store (tickets.md section 3, decision D26).

generated_files.description: Generated outputs exempt from overlap checks like `shared_files`, so a broad docs lease does not block a ticket that regenerates them; unset means the reference pages and schemas, an explicit list (even `[]`) replaces them.

lock_timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for the lease lock before refusing with a timeout.

shared_files.description: Append-shared files exempt from overlap checks; unset means the well-known lockfiles (`Cargo.lock`, `uv.lock`, ...), an explicit list (even `[]`) replaces them.

ttl_secs.description: Seconds a lease stays live after its last renewal (default two hours).

waiter_ttl_secs.description: Seconds a queued `work --wait` waiter may go without a heartbeat before it is dropped (frob:ticket 01M41ZRNYEWRY4V2MXT3WMXBBJ).

mirror.description: Mirror identity settings, so recreate needs no environment variables for them.

bot_ids.description: Logins of the bot accounts whose markers are trusted; empty means the token's own login.

kid.description: Marker signing key id; the key itself stays in `FROB_MIRROR_KEY`.

repo.description: GitHub repository as `OWNER/NAME`; empty means derive it from the `origin` remote.

packs.description: Which data packs the repository enables (packs.md 3.6). Only `local/` packs (atoms) load; external packs and PACK rules do not yet.

enabled.description: Enabled pack ids in load order.

lock.description: Path of the pack lock, relative to the repository root.

severity.description: Repository severity overrides by atom then rule (`[packs.severity]`).

perf.description: The time budget of the built-in rules.

budget_ms.description: Milliseconds the built-in stages of a warm run may take.

enforce.description: Turn an exceeded budget into a Warn finding (`PERF001`).

pm.description: Scrumban policies: pull order, definitions of ready and done, cadence and capacity statistics.

capacity_k.description: Safety factor k in `capacity = rolling_mean - k * stddev` for cycle commitment; 0.5 trades a little throughput for commitments that are usually met.

expedite_max.description: Expedite tickets that may exceed the repository WIP limit at once; 1 lets one critical fix through without opening the floodgates.

intangible_share.description: Largest share (0.0 to 1.0) of a cycle's points that intangible work (chores, debt) may take, checked by PM035; 0.2 keeps upkeep from crowding out features.

cycle_days.description: Days per cycle when a cycle is created without an explicit end; one week is the usual scrumban review cadence.

done_requires.description: Definition of done: predicates checked on close and land; the default lists the three evaluable ones (`criteria_evidenced`, `no_open_children`, `changelog_fragment`); `docs_touched_or_excepted` and `objective_target_met` exist but refuse as Unresolved until they can be evaluated, so listing them is an explicit choice.

max_age_days.description: Ticket aging limits in days per category (`[pm.max_age_days]`); 0 turns a limit off.

in_progress.description: Days a ticket may stay in progress before PM008 fires; 3 keeps work from lingering, 0 is off.

ready.description: Days a ticket may wait in the ready queue (`todo`) before PM008 fires; 30 retires stale intentions, 0 is off.

max_story_points.description: Largest story in points that PM006 accepts; 8 keeps a story finishable within a cycle, 0 turns the check off.

min_history.description: Completed cycles needed before capacity and forecasts are enforced; below it they report Unresolved, so a fresh repository never needs an over-commit.

pull.description: Pull policy; `rank` takes the highest-ranked doable ticket, the only policy so far and the scrumban default.

ready_min.description: Replenishment order point: PM033 advises planning when ready tickets fall below this (default twice the repository WIP limit, so the queue never starves a full WIP).

ready_requires.description: Definition of ready: predicates a ticket must satisfy to enter `ready`; the default is the full list of pm-enforcement.md section 3 so no ill-formed goal is pulled.

sprint_gate.description: Sprint gate: while a cycle is active, `work` and `start` refuse a ticket that is not a member of it (`E-PM-NOT-IN-CYCLE`) unless it is expedite or started with `--unplanned --reason`, which assigns it to the cycle as a recorded over-commit; with no active cycle the gate is silent, so it defaults on.

strict.description: Strict process policy: PM rules that are warnings by default (PM001, PM002, PM008, PM009, PM013, PM034, PM036) become errors, so a repository can make its process gate-enforced; off by default so a fresh repository is only advised.

wip.description: Work-in-progress limits (`[pm.wip]`); 0 turns a limit off.

in_progress.description: Most tickets in progress in the repository at once, sized to what the machine can build; the default 2 matches the two-builder rule, and 0 is off.

in_progress_per_identity.description: Most tickets one holder (actor plus worktree path) may have in progress; 1 makes an agent finish before starting another, 0 is off.

ready.description: Most finished tickets (every criterion bound, evidence passing) waiting to land at once; they leave the `in_progress` count so serial lands do not starve new work, and 0 leaves this column unlimited.

release.description: Release policy knobs read by `frob release status`, `release cut`, `release changelog` and REL001.

fragment_prefix.description: Text `frob ticket fragment` puts before the ticket title in the skeleton (for example `frob: `); empty adds nothing.

preview.description: Products that ship as a preview: their tag message and changelog heading carry " (preview)".

products.description: Products a release ships, one tag each; empty means one product named after the repository.

registry_setup.description: When true, `frob release status` lists frob's own registry setup (trusted publishing on `PyPI` and `crates.io`) as an owner action; false for every other project.

require_ci.description: When true, a CI result that cannot be read (no checks, `gh` missing or unauthenticated, no network, non-GitHub remote) blocks the release like a red one; false reports it as Unresolved only. Unknown is never treated as green.

tag.description: Tag name pattern of a release: `{version}` is required, `{product}` is replaced by each product name (one tag per product).

sync.description: Settings of the freshness probe behind `frob refresh` (`distributed-tickets.md` section 5).

backoff_max_secs.description: Ceiling in seconds of the exponential backoff after failed probes.

foreground_budget_ms.description: Milliseconds a mutating verb may spend probing in the foreground before it falls back to the cache.

probe_timeout_ms.description: Milliseconds before a hung `git ls-remote` is killed.

remote.description: The one authoritative remote; other remotes are never probed.

stale_error_secs.description: Seconds of cache age past which mutating verbs refuse (`E-SYNC-STALE`) when the remote cannot be reached.

ttl_secs.description: Seconds a successful probe stays fresh before the next one is due.

warn_after_secs.description: Seconds of cache age after which read verbs footnote that the ticket view is old.

tests.description: How `frob test` and the `pytest` provider find the Python interpreter (`[tests]`).

non_passing_counts.description: Non-passing pytest outcomes (`skipped`, `xfailed`, `xpassed`) that count as executed tests and so may satisfy evidence; empty (the default) lets none, and they are counted apart either way.

python.description: Interpreter that runs `-m pytest` (a name on `PATH` or a path, relative ones from the repository root); empty uses `.venv` in the repository root when it has one, else `pytest` on `PATH`.

actor.description: Actor recorded on events; empty means git `user.name`.

branch.description: Name of the orphan branch `frob ticket branch init` creates for the ledger (`mirror.md` section 1).

dir.description: Directory of ticket files, relative to the repository root.

good_first_max_points.description: Most points a ticket labelled `good-first` may carry before PM031 fires (`navigation.md` section 4.2).

good_first_min.description: Fewest ready good-first tickets before PM032 warns; 0 turns the rule off (`navigation.md` section 4.2).

handle_min_len.description: Shortest ticket handle shown (`~` plus this many id characters).

index_writer.description: `local`: a parent or title change writes its reindex commit at once; `ci`: it writes only the decision commit and the CI job runs `frob ticket reindex` (`navigation.md` 2.2).

ref.description: Ref holding the ledger; the ledger merge driver and `doctor` resolve it.

ref_mode.description: `trunk` commits to `ref`; `branch` commits to the checked-out branch; `orphan` commits to the ticket branch `branch` in the ticket-branch layout and keeps `ref` as the code base.

types.description: How far Python type annotations are trusted when resolving calls (`docs/design/cohesion.md` 2.2).

trust.description: `checked` (annotations are exact only in files the bound checker ran clean on), `annotated` (claimed, May) or `none` (hints only).

teach.description: Inline explain text: `first` (once per rule, state in `.frob/seen.toml`), `never` (help lines only) or `always`.

dir.description:
Parent directory of ticket worktrees; relative paths resolve against the
primary checkout and `{repo}` stands for its directory name.
